---
title: "E-optimality"
description: "E-optimality limits the worst-estimated direction: the inverse of the smallest eigenvalue of the information matrix."
---

E-optimality limits the worst-estimated direction: the inverse of the smallest eigenvalue of the information matrix.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | Optimal design |
| Direction | Smaller is better |
| Uses a test set | no (a test set given to `optTrain()` is ignored) |
| Score a given set | `eopt_score()` |
| Search with it | `optTrain(method = "EOpt")` |

## Definition

$\mathrm{E} = 1/(\lambda_{\min}(X'X) + \lambda)$. When $p > n$ the smallest eigenvalue is zero and the score is the constant $1/\lambda$, so the criterion does not discriminate between training sets.

## Use in TSDFGS

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
eopt_score(geno[1:50, ])
```

```{r, eval = TRUE}
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "EOpt",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain
```

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see [How the scores are computed](methods.html). Use `min.iter` larger than 300 on real data and check `fit$converged`.

## Original work

Akdemir, D., & Isidro-Sánchez, J. (2019). Design of training populations for selective phenotyping in genomic prediction. *Scientific Reports, 9*, 1446. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-38081-6>

**Repository or website of the original authors:** R package STPGA by Akdemir and colleagues: [CRAN.R-project.org/package=STPGA](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=STPGA) (GPL-3).
